visitedCountriesMap.question: What is the Visited Countries Map and how does it work?
visitedCountriesMap.answer: The Visited Countries Map is a free, browser-first tool for tracking the countries you have travelled to on a single interactive world map. Click the Search button to open the country picker and select a country, or type its name into the picker's search field, and that country is filled in instantly with your chosen colour. Every selection updates your running total, the percentage of the world you have explored, and your continent breakdown in real time. The whole map then animates as a clean, flat world view you can zoom, pan, reset or open in fullscreen — no spreadsheet, no sign-up and nothing to install.

visitedCountriesMap.question: How many countries are there to collect, and how is the percentage of the world calculated?
visitedCountriesMap.answer: The tracker covers 194 sovereign countries across six inhabited continents. Antarctica is deliberately left off the map because it is governed by international treaty rather than being a country, and only the six continents that contain countries are counted, so the card reads “6 of 6 continents” rather than an inflated total. Your exploration percentage is simply the number of countries you have marked divided by 194 — mark 19 countries and you have explored roughly 9.8% of the world — and it updates the moment you select or clear a country.

visitedCountriesMap.question: Is my travel map saved automatically, and will it still be there next time?
visitedCountriesMap.answer: Yes. Every country you mark, along with all of your colours, toggles, name and profile photo, is saved to your browser's own localStorage the instant you make a change, so returning visits restore your map exactly as you left it — there is no save button to remember. Your progress is scoped to the device and browser you used, so it will not appear on a different computer or in a private window. To move it somewhere else, export a JSON backup from the Export menu and import that file on the other device.

visitedCountriesMap.question: Can I share my visited countries map with friends?
visitedCountriesMap.answer: Yes. Open the Share menu to copy a link that carries your selections in the URL itself, so anyone who opens it sees your map already filled in and can build on it themselves. The same menu offers one-click sharing to X, Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp and email. Because the entire map is encoded in the link, no account or server is needed — the recipient simply opens the page and the visited countries are restored.

visitedCountriesMap.question: What export formats does the Visited Countries Map offer?
visitedCountriesMap.answer: The Export menu gives you four formats plus an embed snippet. Download photo card renders a branded, shareable PNG featuring your map, country count, world percentage, continent breakdown and progress bar — complete with your name and profile photo. Download map only exports a clean PNG of the map by itself. Export data (JSON) saves your visited countries and settings as a portable backup you can re-import later, and Download list (CSV) produces a spreadsheet-friendly list of the countries you have visited. Embed code generates an HTML snippet so you can drop your map into a blog or personal site. Exported files are helpfully named, for example visited-countries-alex-carter-map-toolstrek.png.

visitedCountriesMap.question: Can I add my name and a profile photo to the exported card?
visitedCountriesMap.answer: Absolutely — both live in the toolbar above the map. Type your name into the name field and it appears as the headline on your exported photo card. Click the round photo button to open the profile editor, then drag and drop an image or choose a file from your device. You can drag the photo to reposition it and use the zoom slider to choose exactly how much of it shows, guided by a circular crop frame, before saving. The photo is downscaled and stored locally in your browser, never uploaded, and the Customize panel lets you hide it from the card if you prefer.

visitedCountriesMap.question: How do I customize the look of my world map?
visitedCountriesMap.answer: Open the Customize panel to restyle the map without touching your data. You can pick a one-click colour theme such as Classic Blue or Midnight, or set the visited colour, unvisited country colour, border colour, ocean/background colour, border width and unvisited opacity individually. You can also toggle country names, grid lines, the world percentage badge, the legend, and “highlight visited” emphasis, or hide the profile photo and stats on the exported card. Every change previews live on the map and is saved with your progress.

visitedCountriesMap.question: Does the Visited Countries Map work on mobile and offline?
visitedCountriesMap.answer: Yes. The layout is fully responsive and touch-friendly: the toolbar collapses into neat rows, the map fills its frame without ever being cut off, the country picker becomes a scrollable modal, and you can tap to mark countries and pinch or pan to explore, with zoom, reset and fullscreen controls always within reach. Because the map is generated inside your browser, once the page has loaded you can keep marking countries even with a flaky connection.

visitedCountriesMap.question: Is the Visited Countries Map private, and how do I reset it?
visitedCountriesMap.answer: It is completely private. Your selections, settings, name and profile photo are handled entirely client-side and stored only in your own browser — nothing is uploaded, tracked or shared. To start over, click Reset in the toolbar beside Customize and confirm: this clears your visited countries, your photo and every customisation from this device in one step. If you only want to unmark a country, reopen the picker and click it again — the same click that selects a country also deselects it.

ageOnOtherPlanets.question: How does the Age on Other Planets calculator work?
ageOnOtherPlanets.answer: It first works out exactly how many Earth days you have been alive — from your birth date to the “as of” date you choose — then divides that number by each planet's orbital period. Mercury completes an orbit in 87.97 days, Venus in 224.70, Earth in 365.25, Mars in 686.98, Jupiter in 4,332.59, Saturn in 10,759.22, Uranus in 30,688.5, Neptune in 60,190 and Pluto in 90,560 Earth days. The result is your age in that planet's years, calculated to the day.

ageOnOtherPlanets.question: How old am I on Mars?
ageOnOtherPlanets.answer: A Mars year lasts about 687 Earth days — nearly two Earth years — so your Martian age is roughly half your Earth age. If you are 30 on Earth you are about 15.9 Mars years old, and you have lived around 10,600 Martian sols, because one sol (a Mars day) is only 39 minutes longer than an Earth day.

ageOnOtherPlanets.question: Why is my age different on every planet?
ageOnOtherPlanets.answer: A “year” is simply one full trip around the Sun, and each planet completes that trip at a different speed and distance. Mercury races around in 88 days while Neptune takes almost 165 Earth years, so your age in planet-years measures how many orbits you have completed on that world. You are oldest on Mercury — about 4.15 Mercury years for every Earth year — and youngest on Neptune.

ageOnOtherPlanets.question: What is a planetary birthday, and when is my next one?
ageOnOtherPlanets.answer: A planetary birthday (also called a solar return) happens when the planet returns to the position it held when you were born, completing another full orbit. The tool tracks your progress toward the next one on every world with a live progress bar, shows the exact Earth date it falls on and how many days away it is, and lets you plan milestone birthdays — your 10th, 50th, 100th or any custom number — in the Milestone planner.

ageOnOtherPlanets.question: How do you work out my weight and jump height on other planets?
ageOnOtherPlanets.answer: Surface gravity ranges from 0.063 g on Pluto to 2.53 g on Jupiter. Switch on the Weight & jump module, enter your Earth weight and a typical jump, and the calculator multiplies your weight by each planet's gravity — about 2.5× heavier on Jupiter and roughly 16× lighter on Pluto — while your jump height is divided by the same gravity, because weaker gravity lets you jump higher.

ageOnOtherPlanets.question: Is Pluto included, and can I choose which planets to show?
ageOnOtherPlanets.answer: Pluto is included as a dwarf planet so you can see just how long its 248-Earth-year orbit really is. Every world — the eight planets and Pluto — can be toggled on or off in the Customise panel, and the cards, comparison table, milestone planner and exports all follow your selection.

ageOnOtherPlanets.question: Does the calculator handle leap-day birthdays and future dates?
ageOnOtherPlanets.answer: Yes. The maths runs on whole Earth days rather than calendar years, so a February 29 birthday needs no special handling. You can also move the “as of” date to any day after your birth — including a future date — to project your cosmic age at that moment.

ageOnOtherPlanets.question: Can I share or export my cosmic birthday report?
ageOnOtherPlanets.answer: Yes. Copy a ready-made text summary, copy a share link that restores your dates and settings, download a branded PNG report card listing your age on every selected world, or export the full comparison as CSV or JSON. Units, decimal precision and visible planets are all captured in the exports, and every file is generated in your browser.

ageOnOtherPlanets.question: Is my birth date stored or uploaded anywhere?
ageOnOtherPlanets.answer: Never. The calculator runs 100% client-side. Your birth date and preferences are saved only in your own browser's localStorage so the tool can remember them, and a share link keeps the dates in the URL you control. Nothing is sent to a server, logged or tracked.

dogCatAgeCalculator.question: How does the Dog & Cat Age Calculator work?
dogCatAgeCalculator.answer: It first works out exactly how many Earth days your pet has been alive — from their birthday to the “as of” date you choose — then converts that real age into human years with the method you select. The default size-aware chart counts 15 human years for the first pet year, adds 9 for the second, then adds a yearly rate based on species and size: about 4 per year for cats and small dogs, 5 for medium dogs, 6 for large dogs and 7 for giant dogs. The report also covers life stage, typical lifespan, next birthday, milestone birthdays and lifetime statistics.

dogCatAgeCalculator.question: How old is my dog in human years?
dogCatAgeCalculator.answer: A medium dog is roughly 24 human years old at age two, then gains about five human years for every additional dog year, so a 5-year-old medium dog is around 39. Size matters: small breeds gain about four years per dog year while giant breeds gain closer to seven. Choose your dog's size — or enter a weight and apply the suggested class — for an accurate conversion.

dogCatAgeCalculator.question: How old is my cat in human years?
dogCatAgeCalculator.answer: Cats follow a similar early curve: the first year counts as about 15 human years and the second brings them to roughly 24, after which each cat year adds around four. A 10-year-old cat is therefore about 56 in human years and a 15-year-old cat about 76. Indoor cats commonly live 13–17 years, while outdoor-only cats average far less.

dogCatAgeCalculator.question: Is the “multiply by 7” rule accurate?
dogCatAgeCalculator.answer: No — it is a handy shortcut, not a scientific formula. Pets mature much faster than humans in their first two years, and lifespan varies with species, adult size and lifestyle. The calculator keeps the classic 7× rule as a comparison option, but the size-aware chart is a much better reflection of how dogs and cats actually age.

dogCatAgeCalculator.question: Why does a dog's size change the conversion?
dogCatAgeCalculator.answer: Adult size is one of the strongest predictors of canine lifespan. Small breeds commonly live 12–16 years, medium breeds 11–14, large breeds 9–12 and giant breeds 7–10, and larger bodies tend to age faster at a cellular level. That is why the tool uses a different yearly conversion rate for each size class, and why a giant dog can be a senior at six while a small dog may not be senior until nine or ten.

dogCatAgeCalculator.question: Does my cat's lifestyle really affect life expectancy?
dogCatAgeCalculator.answer: It is one of the biggest factors in feline life expectancy. Indoor cats commonly reach 13–17 years, cats with some outdoor access average around 10–14, and outdoor-only cats often live only 5–10 years because of traffic, predators, weather and infectious disease. The lifestyle choice shapes the lifespan estimate without changing the age conversion itself.

dogCatAgeCalculator.question: What if I don't know my pet's exact birthday, or they were born on February 29?
dogCatAgeCalculator.answer: If you are not sure of the exact date, open “Estimate from age”, enter your pet's age in years and months, and the calculator works backwards from the “as of” date to create an approximate birthday. Pets born on February 29 are handled cleanly: their age and next birthday use February 28 in non-leap years, so nothing ever shifts by a day or breaks.

dogCatAgeCalculator.question: Can I share or export my pet's report, and is the data private?
dogCatAgeCalculator.answer: Yes. Copy a text summary, copy a share link that restores every setting, download a branded PNG report card, or export the full report as CSV or JSON — all generated in your browser. Names, birthdays and preferences are saved only in your own browser's localStorage and in links you create yourself; nothing is uploaded, logged or tracked.

imageWatermark.question: How does the Image Watermark tool work?
imageWatermark.answer: The Image Watermark tool adds text or logo watermarks to images entirely in your browser. You can customise font, size, color, opacity, position, rotation, tiling, blend modes, stroke and shadow, then export as PNG, JPEG or WebP. Images never leave your device.

collageMaker.question: How does the Collage Maker work?
collageMaker.answer: The Collage Maker combines multiple images into grid, masonry or polaroid layouts. You can adjust columns, spacing, corner radius, image fit, background (solid or gradient) and shadows, drag to reorder images, then download the result as a PNG all client-side.

imageEditor.question: How does the Image Editor work?
imageEditor.answer: The Image Editor applies professional filters and adjustments - brightness, contrast, saturation, hue, sepia, grayscale, invert, blur, temperature, tint, exposure, gamma, vignette and noise - plus rotate and flip transforms. Export as PNG, JPEG or WebP. Everything runs in your browser.

flightDurationCalculator.question: How does the Flight Duration Calculator handle time zones and daylight saving?
flightDurationCalculator.answer: Every airport in the catalogue is paired with an IANA time zone. The calculator converts the local departure and arrival times into UTC before subtracting them, so time-zone shifts never distort the flight time. Because the browser's time-zone database is used for the exact travel date, daylight saving changes, half-hour offsets and 45-minute offsets are applied automatically. If a local time is skipped or repeated during a clock change, the tool uses the nearest valid instant and shows a clear warning instead of returning a silent error.

flightDurationCalculator.question: What is the difference between flight time, gate-to-gate time and door-to-door time?
flightDurationCalculator.answer: Flight time is the airborne time from take-off to landing. Gate-to-gate time is the elapsed time from the first departure to the final arrival, so it includes every layover. Door-to-door time adds your pre-departure airport buffer and post-arrival buffer on top. The results panel shows all three separately, and you can choose whether the large headline number uses gate-to-gate or door-to-door time in the Advanced options.

flightDurationCalculator.question: Can I calculate an arrival or departure time when one of them is unknown?
flightDurationCalculator.answer: Yes. The tool has three modes. Flight duration mode uses known departure and arrival times to calculate the flight time. Arrival time mode takes a departure time and flight duration and returns the exact local arrival time at the destination, including date changes. Departure time mode does the reverse: enter the required arrival time and duration, and it works backwards to the local departure time you need.

flightDurationCalculator.question: How does the calculator evaluate connections and layover risk?
flightDurationCalculator.answer: For each connection it subtracts the previous arrival from the next departure and compares the gap with the minimum connection time you set for domestic and international transfers. Below-minimum gaps are flagged, gaps just above the minimum are marked tight, and unusually long waits are marked as long layovers. A negative gap or a connection under 15 minutes is treated as an error because the itinerary cannot physically work. You can adjust the domestic and international minimums to match your own comfort level.

flightDurationCalculator.question: Does the Flight Duration Calculator support multi-city trips and custom airports?
flightDurationCalculator.answer: Yes. In Flight duration mode you can add up to six flights, each with its own airports, local departure and arrival times, airline and flight number. The tool calculates every leg, every layover and the complete journey. The searchable airport catalogue covers more than 100 major airports, and the Custom airport option lets you enter any airport manually and choose its IANA time zone for accurate conversion.

flightDurationCalculator.question: Is my itinerary private and can I export the result?
flightDurationCalculator.answer: Everything runs 100% in your browser. Airport choices, dates, airline names and results are never uploaded, logged or sent to a server. You can copy a complete text itinerary to your clipboard or download a formatted PDF report from the results panel. The PDF includes each flight, local times, time-zone offsets, layovers, buffers and any warnings.

passportPhotoMaker.question: Is this passport photo maker safe for personal photos?
passportPhotoMaker.answer: Yes. The photo is decoded, cropped, analysed and exported entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. No image, face data or measurement ever leaves your device, and nothing is stored after you close the page.

passportPhotoMaker.question: Does the tool guarantee my photo will be accepted?
passportPhotoMaker.answer: No tool can guarantee acceptance because the final decision belongs to the passport office or embassy. The readiness score checks what can be measured digitally — resolution, background uniformity, lighting, contrast and framing — and the presets follow published guidance. Always confirm the current rules with the issuing authority before printing.

passportPhotoMaker.question: Which file format should I use for printing?
passportPhotoMaker.answer: JPEG at 300 DPI is the safest choice for photo labs and home printers. PNG is useful when you need a transparent matte, but most passport authorities require a plain background, so a JPEG is usually better. PDF is ideal when you want a correctly sized print sheet with several copies.

passportPhotoMaker.question: Why does my background check show a warning?
passportPhotoMaker.answer: The checker samples the outer edge of your cropped photo. A wall with shadows, a door frame or hair touching the edge can lower the score. Move to even, soft lighting and leave space around your head. The check is a helpful signal, not a judgement by the passport office.

passportPhotoMaker.question: Can I use a phone selfie?
passportPhotoMaker.answer: Often yes, if the photo is sharp, taken from eye level at a neutral distance, and lit evenly from the front. Avoid wide-angle distortion, beauty filters, heavy HDR and flash shadows. A rear camera on a timer usually gives better resolution and less distortion than a front camera.

passportPhotoMaker.question: How many copies fit on a print sheet?
passportPhotoMaker.answer: The tool calculates this automatically from the photo size, paper size, margin and gap. A 4 × 6 inch sheet commonly fits six or more 35 × 45 mm photos, while A4 can fit many more. The maximum printed copies is shown before you download the PDF.

meetingTimePlanner.question: How does the Meeting Time Planner find the best time?
meetingTimePlanner.answer: For every candidate slot it converts the same instant into each participant's local time using the IANA time-zone database. A slot earns the highest score when everybody is inside their working hours, loses points when someone is early, late, outside hours, asleep or on a weekend, and loses a small amount when the meeting lands on a different calendar date for part of the group. The highest-scoring slots are ranked, and the day map highlights the best option in every hour.

meetingTimePlanner.question: Does it handle daylight saving time and half-hour offsets?
meetingTimePlanner.answer: Yes. The conversion uses each participant's IANA zone for the actual meeting date, so daylight saving, half-hour offsets such as India, 45-minute offsets such as Nepal, and date-line crossings are all applied automatically. If a local wall time does not exist because of a spring-forward change, the planner moves to the nearest valid instant and still returns a usable slot.

meetingTimePlanner.question: What should I do when no time works for everyone?
meetingTimePlanner.answer: That is common for genuinely global teams. Turn off the 'Only perfect overlaps' filter, then compare the ranked compromises: the score, the number of people inside working hours, and the local time for each participant make the trade-off visible. Rotating the inconvenient slot between regions, shortening the meeting, or recording it for one participant are all fairer long-term solutions than asking the same person to join at midnight every time.

meetingTimePlanner.question: How do working hours and weekends affect the score?
meetingTimePlanner.answer: You can set a shared working window such as 09:00–17:00, choose which weekdays count, and use the meeting duration when checking the end time. A meeting that starts inside working hours but runs past the end is marked late. Weekends and nights carry larger penalties. The default sample deliberately spans New York, London, Dubai and Berlin, so it often has no perfect overlap and shows how the tool surfaces the best compromise instead of hiding it.

meetingTimePlanner.question: Can I export the meeting to my calendar?
meetingTimePlanner.answer: Yes. Select a slot and download a standards-compliant .ics invite with the correct UTC start and end times, participants, local times and a description. It imports into Google Calendar, Outlook, Apple Calendar and most other calendar apps. You can also copy a plain-text summary for chat or email.

meetingTimePlanner.question: Is my meeting information private?
meetingTimePlanner.answer: Completely. Participant names, time zones, dates and results are processed in your browser with the built-in Intl APIs. Nothing is uploaded, logged or saved on a server, and there is no account or tracking. Closing the tab clears the meeting.

fuelCostCalculator.question: How is the fuel cost calculated?
fuelCostCalculator.answer: The calculator converts your distance and efficiency into a single metric fuel figure, then applies your driving-style and load adjustments. For example, 1,000 km at 7.5 L/100 km uses 75 litres. Multiplying 75 litres by the price per litre gives the fuel cost. Tolls, parking, accommodation and food are added afterwards to produce the complete trip cost.

fuelCostCalculator.question: Does the calculator account for a round trip?
fuelCostCalculator.answer: Yes. Turn on Round trip and the one-way distance is doubled. The fuel, cost, driving time and emissions figures all use the full distance, while the distance field stays as the one-way value so it is easy to compare routes.

fuelCostCalculator.question: Why is my real-world fuel use higher than the result?
fuelCostCalculator.answer: No calculator can predict traffic, weather, tyre pressure, air-conditioning, altitude or driving style exactly. Use the advanced driving-style and load selectors to add a realistic allowance, and treat the answer as a planning estimate. Keeping a small cash buffer is always sensible on a long drive.

fuelCostCalculator.question: How does the cost-per-person split work?
fuelCostCalculator.answer: The total of fuel and every extra cost is divided by the number of passengers. It assumes an even split. If one person is driving more, or someone joins for only part of the trip, use the per-person figure as a starting point and adjust the split manually.

fuelCostCalculator.question: What do the fuel stops and range figures mean?
fuelCostCalculator.answer: Full-tank range is the distance you can cover on the usable part of a full tank, after excluding your reserve. The fuel-stop estimate starts from your chosen starting fuel level and assumes each stop fills the usable tank. It is a planning aid, not a guarantee that stations will be available exactly where you need them.

fuelCostCalculator.question: Is the trip data private?
fuelCostCalculator.answer: Yes. Every calculation happens in your browser and no route, price, budget or personal detail is uploaded. There is no account, no tracking pixel and no server-side storage. Closing or refreshing the page clears the trip.

fuelCostCalculator.question: Can I export the estimate?
fuelCostCalculator.answer: Yes. Copy a plain-text summary for a message or notes app, or download a CSV file that opens in Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets. The CSV includes the distance, fuel use, costs, per-person split, drive time, emissions, fuel stops and budget comparison.

uuidUlidGenerator.question: What is the difference between UUID v4, v7 and ULID?
uuidUlidGenerator.answer: UUID v4 is 122 random bits with no timestamp, so values are opaque and cannot be sorted by creation time. UUID v7 puts a 48-bit Unix millisecond timestamp first and fills the rest with 74 random bits, making it sortable while remaining globally unique. ULID uses the same millisecond prefix but encodes the whole value in 26 Crockford Base32 characters with 80 random bits, so it is shorter to read and naturally case-insensitive.

uuidUlidGenerator.question: Are these identifiers generated securely?
uuidUlidGenerator.answer: Yes. Random values come from crypto.getRandomValues(), which uses the operating system's cryptographically secure random number generator. There is no Math.random fallback. UUID v5 uses the Web Crypto SHA-1 digest exactly as the RFC specifies; SHA-1 is used here as a deterministic name mapping, not as a password security primitive.

uuidUlidGenerator.question: Can two generated identifiers collide?
uuidUlidGenerator.answer: The chance is astronomically small for random UUIDs, ULIDs and well-sized NanoIDs. A UUID v4 has 122 random bits, a ULID has 80 random bits per millisecond and a 21-character NanoID over a 64-character alphabet has about 126 bits. The collision estimate in the output panel shows the pairwise probability for the batch you generated.

uuidUlidGenerator.question: What does monotonic mean for ULID?
uuidUlidGenerator.answer: Standard ULIDs generated in the same millisecond may sort randomly because each one has an independent random tail. With monotonic output enabled, each additional ULID in the same batch increments the previous random tail, so the whole batch sorts in creation order. The timestamp still comes first.

uuidUlidGenerator.question: When should I use UUID v5?
uuidUlidGenerator.answer: UUID v5 is for deterministic mapping, not for secrets. Given the same namespace and name, it always returns the same UUID. That is useful for stable integration IDs, deduplicating records or mapping a domain name to an identifier. Because the output is predictable, never use UUID v5 where an unguessable token is required.

uuidUlidGenerator.question: Are time-based identifiers private?
uuidUlidGenerator.answer: UUID v1, UUID v7 and ULID all reveal an approximate creation timestamp. That is often useful for debugging and database ordering, but it can leak when a record was created. UUID v4 and random NanoIDs do not contain a timestamp. This generator never embeds a hardware MAC address: UUID v1 uses a random node identifier with the multicast bit set.

uuidUlidGenerator.question: Is anything uploaded or stored?
uuidUlidGenerator.answer: No. Generation, formatting, validation and downloads happen entirely in your browser. There is no API call, account or analytics event for the identifiers. Refreshing the page discards the current batch.

pregnancyDueDateCalculator.question: How is the pregnancy due date calculated?
pregnancyDueDateCalculator.answer: The most common method is Naegele's rule: add 280 days (40 weeks) to the first day of your last menstrual period. If your cycle is longer or shorter than 28 days, the calculator adjusts the date by the difference. A known conception date uses 266 days, an ultrasound uses the measured gestational age, and IVF uses a fixed offset based on embryo age.

pregnancyDueDateCalculator.question: Why does my cycle length change the due date?
pregnancyDueDateCalculator.answer: Naegele's rule assumes ovulation on day 14 of a 28-day cycle. If your cycle is 32 days, ovulation is typically later, so the calculator adds 4 days. A 26-day cycle moves the due date 2 days earlier. This is still an estimate; an early dating scan can refine it.

pregnancyDueDateCalculator.question: What is the difference between gestational age and fetal age?
pregnancyDueDateCalculator.answer: Gestational age is counted from the first day of the last period, even though conception happens about two weeks later. Fetal or embryonic age is counted from conception, so it is usually about 14 days less than gestational age. Pregnancy care almost always uses gestational age.

pregnancyDueDateCalculator.question: How accurate is an ultrasound due date?
pregnancyDueDateCalculator.answer: An early first-trimester scan is usually accurate to within about 5–7 days, and sometimes closer. Later scans are less precise for dating because babies grow at different rates. This calculator simply converts the scan's reported weeks and days into an estimated 40-week due date.

pregnancyDueDateCalculator.question: How does IVF transfer dating work?
pregnancyDueDateCalculator.answer: For a day-5 blastocyst transfer, the due date is 261 days after the transfer (266 minus 5). Day-3 and day-6 transfers use 263 and 260 days. This relies on the transfer date and embryo age provided by your fertility clinic, which is usually more precise than LMP dating.

pregnancyDueDateCalculator.question: What do the milestone dates mean?
pregnancyDueDateCalculator.answer: Milestones are typical gestational windows for screening, scans and trimester boundaries, not personalised medical instructions. Your care team may schedule appointments differently based on your history, local guidelines and the results of earlier tests.

pregnancyDueDateCalculator.question: Is my information private and is this medical advice?
pregnancyDueDateCalculator.answer: Yes, every date is calculated in your browser and nothing is uploaded. This tool provides educational estimates only and does not replace medical advice. Always confirm your due date and care schedule with a qualified healthcare professional.

imageCropper.question: How does the Image Cropper protect my photos?
imageCropper.answer: Your image is decoded locally by the browser into a canvas, cropped at the exact source pixels and re-encoded on your device. Nothing is uploaded to a server, there is no tracking and the file disappears from memory when you close the tab.

imageCropper.question: Does cropping reduce image quality?
imageCropper.answer: The crop is rendered from the original image at its native resolution, not from the on-screen preview, so no detail is lost. PNG exports are lossless; JPEG and WebP exports use the quality slider, and 90–95% is a good balance between sharpness and file size.

imageCropper.question: What is the difference between the crop box and image zoom?
imageCropper.answer: The crop box selects the part of the photo you keep. Zoom magnifies the photo beneath the box so you can place it precisely, and Pan lets you slide that magnified image. Cropping still uses the original resolution no matter how far you zoom in.

imageCropper.question: Can I straighten a tilted photo?
imageCropper.answer: Yes. Rotate in exact 90-degree steps, flip horizontally or vertically, or use the straighten slider between −15 and +15 degrees. All transforms are baked into the working canvas before cropping, so you never get transparent or missing corners.

imageCropper.question: Which aspect ratio should I use for social media?
imageCropper.answer: Choose a social preset and the tool sets both the ratio and a recommended output width — 1080 × 1080 for an Instagram post, 1080 × 1920 for a story or Reel, 1280 × 720 for a YouTube thumbnail, and more. You can still fine-tune the crop and output size afterwards.

imageCropper.question: Why does JPEG ask for a background colour?
imageCropper.answer: JPEG does not support transparency. If the cropped area contains transparent pixels they are filled with the matte colour you choose, white by default. PNG and WebP keep transparency, so the matte option is hidden for those formats.

imageCropper.question: Can I crop a screenshot from my clipboard?
imageCropper.answer: Yes. Copy an image, then press Ctrl/Cmd + V anywhere on the page. You can also drag a file onto the drop zone or browse your device; JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF and AVIF files up to 40 MB are supported.

invoiceGenerator.question: Is the Invoice Generator really free?
invoiceGenerator.answer: Yes. Unlimited invoices, PDF export, printing, 40 currencies, logo upload, templates and JSON drafts are all free with no account needed. The entire tool runs in your browser, so client and payment details never reach a server.

invoiceGenerator.question: Can I save an invoice and edit it later?
invoiceGenerator.answer: Your current invoice is auto-saved in this browser using local storage. For a portable backup, use Export draft to download a JSON file and import it later on any device. Clearing site data or using a different browser starts a fresh draft.

invoiceGenerator.question: What is the difference between exclusive and inclusive tax?
invoiceGenerator.answer: Exclusive tax is added on top of your prices: a 100.00 line with 20% VAT becomes 120.00. Inclusive tax extracts the tax already contained in the price: a 120.00 line at 20% includes 20.00 of VAT. Switch modes in Invoice details and every total recalculates instantly.

invoiceGenerator.question: Can I add my own logo and brand colour?
invoiceGenerator.answer: Yes. Upload a PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG logo (it is converted to print-safe PNG locally) and pick one of six accent colours. Both appear in the live preview and the generated PDF, and you can hide the logo without deleting it.

invoiceGenerator.question: Does the PDF handle many line items?
invoiceGenerator.answer: Yes. The vector PDF engine paginates automatically, repeats the table header on each new page, keeps totals and payment details together and adds page numbers in the footer. Choose Compact layout for tighter spacing on long invoices.

invoiceGenerator.question: Which currencies and number formats are supported?
invoiceGenerator.answer: Forty currencies with locale-aware symbols, grouping and decimal rules, from USD, EUR and GBP to BDT, INR, NGN and JPY. The PDF prints ISO currency codes so amounts render correctly in every PDF reader.

invoiceGenerator.question: Is the generated invoice legally valid?
invoiceGenerator.answer: The document includes the usual fields — a unique invoice number, issue and due dates, seller and buyer details, tax IDs, itemised lines, tax breakdown and payment terms — but legal requirements vary by country. Check your local rules and keep your own records.

urlEncoderDecoder.question: What is the difference between encodeURIComponent and encodeURI?
urlEncoderDecoder.answer: encodeURIComponent escapes every character that is not unreserved, including reserved characters such as / ? & = and #. Use it for a single value. encodeURI leaves reserved characters untouched so a complete URL keeps its structure. In ToolsTrek, choose Component or Full URL to switch between them.

urlEncoderDecoder.question: Why does a space sometimes become + and sometimes %20?
urlEncoderDecoder.answer: In application/x-www-form-urlencoded data — classic HTML form submissions — spaces are represented by + and a literal plus is written as %2B. Inside a normal URL path or query value a space is %20. The Form data mode performs the + substitution; the other modes keep %20.

urlEncoderDecoder.question: Is the URL Encoder safe for sensitive data?
urlEncoderDecoder.answer: Yes. Encoding and decoding run entirely in your browser with JavaScript, so URLs, tokens and form values never leave your device. There is no upload, logging or server round-trip on this page.

urlEncoderDecoder.question: What happens to malformed escapes such as 100%?
urlEncoderDecoder.answer: A standard decodeURIComponent call throws a URIError and stops processing the whole string. ToolsTrek uses a tolerant decoder that preserves invalid sequences exactly as typed, counts them and decodes every valid %XX sequence around them, so 100% off stays readable.

urlEncoderDecoder.question: Can I encode or decode a list of values line by line?
urlEncoderDecoder.answer: Yes. Enable Process each line and every line is encoded or decoded independently while the original line breaks are preserved. This is ideal for keyword lists, tracking parameters and bulk redirect maps.

urlEncoderDecoder.question: Does the Query Builder handle Unicode and empty values?
urlEncoderDecoder.answer: Yes. Query Builder encodes keys and values with the same engine, supports Unicode and emoji, keeps empty values as key=, can sort keys alphabetically for stable signatures and can import an existing query string into editable rows.

urlEncoderDecoder.question: How do I encode a URL for a share link or email?
urlEncoderDecoder.answer: Use Full URL mode for the destination, then Component mode on that encoded URL if it is being placed inside another parameter — for example share?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com. The Inspector panel shows the decoded parts so you can confirm the result.

wheelSpinner.question: How does the Wheel Spinner choose a winner?
wheelSpinner.answer: Every spin uses the Web Crypto API (crypto.getRandomValues). Weighted mode gives each option a chance proportional to its weight, while Equal mode ignores weights. The winning segment is selected before the animation starts, so the pointer always lands on the real result.

wheelSpinner.question: Why does the wheel start empty?
wheelSpinner.answer: ToolsTrek never inserts sample options into your workspace. Add options one at a time, paste a bulk list, or press Load demo data to explore the tool. An empty wheel stays empty until you add something, and nothing is saved to a server.

wheelSpinner.question: Can I customise weights, colours and probability?
wheelSpinner.answer: Yes. Every option has an editable weight and colour, and you can switch between Weighted and Equal probability modes. Six palettes recolour the wheel instantly, while individual rows can override the palette colour. Weight 2 is twice as likely as weight 1.

wheelSpinner.question: Can I export a wheel or its results?
wheelSpinner.answer: Yes. Export the wheel as JSON or CSV, import a JSON wheel, and download the full spin history as CSV. The winner card also has a one-click copy action, and all data is stored only in your browser localStorage.

randomPicker.question: What can the Random Picker do?
randomPicker.answer: It draws one winner, picks several names without repeats, shuffles an entire list, splits items into balanced teams with a snake draft, or generates unique random numbers inside a range. Weighted draws are available for single and multi-winner modes.

randomPicker.question: Is the Random Picker different from the Wheel Spinner?
randomPicker.answer: Both use the same cryptographically secure random engine, but the picker is built for larger lists and more formats. The wheel is a visual single-winner raffle; the picker adds pick-N sampling, full shuffles, team building, number ranges and duplicate filtering.

randomPicker.question: Why is the item list empty at the start?
randomPicker.answer: No sample names are pre-loaded. Add items individually, paste a bulk list, or press Load demo data to try the tool. The demo only fills the list after you click it and never performs a draw automatically.

randomPicker.question: Where are my items and results stored?
randomPicker.answer: Items, settings and draw history live in this browser localStorage only. You can export or import the pool as JSON, download results and history as CSV, and clear everything at any time.

coinFlipDice.question: Is the Coin Flip & Dice tool truly random?
coinFlipDice.answer: Yes. Every flip and roll uses crypto.getRandomValues rather than Math.random. The outcome is chosen before the animation plays, so the displayed result always matches the secure draw. A fair coin gives each side an exact 50% chance.

coinFlipDice.question: Can I change the coin faces and odds?
coinFlipDice.answer: Yes. Add, rename, recolour or delete faces, and give each side a relative weight. Weighted mode honours those weights; Fair mode ignores them and treats every side equally. At least two sides are required.

coinFlipDice.question: Which dice can I roll?
coinFlipDice.answer: Use the d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20 or d100 presets, or type any number of sides from 2 to 1000. Roll up to 20 dice at once, add a flat modifier, and use advantage or disadvantage to roll the pool twice and keep the higher or lower total.

coinFlipDice.question: Does the tool save my coins and history?
coinFlipDice.answer: Your coin faces, rules and session history are stored in this browser localStorage. Export the configuration as JSON or the history as CSV at any time. Clearing site data removes everything permanently.

screenRecorder.question: How does the Screen Recorder work?
screenRecorder.answer: It uses the browser getDisplayMedia API to capture a screen, window or tab, then records the stream with MediaRecorder. Audio from the shared source and your microphone are mixed through Web Audio into one track. The finished file is assembled in memory and downloaded locally.

screenRecorder.question: Which browsers support screen recording with audio?
screenRecorder.answer: Chromium desktop browsers such as Chrome, Edge and Opera offer the best support, including tab audio. Firefox supports screen capture but system audio depends on the operating system. Safari support is limited. The tool lists only the output codecs your browser reports as supported.

screenRecorder.question: Can I add a webcam, clock or watermark?
screenRecorder.answer: Yes. When the webcam overlay is enabled, the screen is painted to an offscreen canvas at your chosen resolution and the camera is drawn as a circular picture-in-picture bubble. The same canvas pipeline can burn in a live clock and a Toolstrek watermark.

screenRecorder.question: Are my recordings uploaded or stored?
screenRecorder.answer: No. Recordings exist only as temporary blob URLs in this browser tab and disappear when you reload or close the page. There is no upload, no server storage and no account. Download anything you want to keep.

videoTrimmer.question: Does the Video Trimmer upload my file?
videoTrimmer.answer: Never. The file is read locally with the File API, decoded and encoded with WebCodecs through MediaBunny, and written to memory as a new blob. No byte is sent over the network, and the tool keeps working offline once the page has loaded.

videoTrimmer.question: Is trimming lossless?
videoTrimmer.answer: Precise trimming re-encodes only the frames inside the selected range so the cut is frame accurate and starts exactly at your in point. Re-encoding introduces a small generation loss, so choose a higher bitrate if you plan to edit the result again.

videoTrimmer.question: Which input and output formats are supported?
videoTrimmer.answer: You can open MP4, WebM, MKV, MOV and most common containers, plus audio files such as MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG and FLAC. Export video to MP4, WebM or MKV, or audio-only to M4A, MP3, WAV or OGG.

videoTrimmer.question: What is the demo clip button for?
videoTrimmer.answer: It draws a 10-second animated test card on a canvas and records it with MediaRecorder entirely on your device. The generated clip is a normal video file, so you can practise setting in and out points and exporting before using your own footage.

voiceRecorder.question: How does the Voice Recorder work?
voiceRecorder.answer: The tool captures your microphone with the browser getUserMedia API and records it using MediaRecorder. Audio stays in memory as a blob URL, so playback and downloads happen entirely on your device. Choose WebM, OGG, M4A or WAV before you start recording.

voiceRecorder.question: Is anything uploaded to a server?
voiceRecorder.answer: No. Microphone audio, camera frames, snapshots and recordings never leave your device. The page makes no upload request and does not require an account. Closing or reloading the tab permanently discards the session.

voiceRecorder.question: What can the Mic Test measure?
voiceRecorder.answer: The mic test shows a live oscilloscope, RMS and peak levels in decibels, an approximate noise floor, clipping events and a signal-quality score. It also lets you switch input devices so you can compare headset and built-in microphones before recording.

voiceRecorder.question: Why does my camera preview stay blank?
voiceRecorder.answer: Browsers only grant camera access on HTTPS or localhost, and the permission must be allowed for this site. If another application is already using the camera, close it and press Start camera again. The demo feed button shows a synthetic test pattern without using your camera.

voiceRecorder.question: What is the demo data button for?
voiceRecorder.answer: Every field starts empty. Load demo audio to hear a locally synthesised melody and try the playback, rename and download controls. The demo camera feed draws a moving test card on a canvas, so you can explore the layout without granting permissions.

voiceRecorder.question: Which recording format should I choose?
voiceRecorder.answer: WebM Opus is the smallest and works in Chrome, Edge and Firefox. M4A AAC plays natively on Apple devices. WAV is lossless and accepted everywhere, but files are much larger. The tool only lists formats your browser can encode, and WAV is generated locally from the recorded audio.

memeGenerator.question: How does the Meme Generator work?
memeGenerator.answer: Upload an image or start with a blank canvas, then add as many text layers as you need. Each layer supports drag positioning, font, size, colour, gradient fill, outline, shadow, highlight box, rotation, opacity, alignment and letter spacing. The canvas is rendered at full resolution in your browser and exported as PNG, JPEG or WebP.

memeGenerator.question: Are my images uploaded anywhere?
memeGenerator.answer: No. Images are read with the File API, drawn onto an HTML canvas and exported locally. Nothing is sent to a server, no account is required, and closing the tab discards the session. The editor also works offline after the page loads.

memeGenerator.question: Can I save my meme and come back later?
memeGenerator.answer: Yes. The project autosaves to this browser local storage, including text layers and the background image where space allows. You can also export a .json project file and import it later on another device. Export JSON is available in the Export panel.

memeGenerator.question: Why does the demo button exist?
memeGenerator.answer: Every field starts blank so nothing is pre-filled for you. Load demo data to see a complete gradient layout with two styled captions, then edit or delete it. The demo is generated locally and does not use an external image.

memeGenerator.question: Which export size should I pick?
memeGenerator.answer: Use 1x for quick sharing, 2x for crisp social posts and 3x for print or large displays. The canvas base size is shown in the Size panel, so a 1080 x 1080 project at 2x exports a 2160 x 2160 PNG.

memeGenerator.question: Can I move text with the keyboard?
memeGenerator.answer: Yes. Select a text layer and press the arrow keys to nudge it by one pixel, or hold Shift for ten pixels. Delete removes the selected layer and Escape clears the selection. Dragging directly on the canvas also works on touch screens and with a mouse.

videoToGif.question: How does the Video to GIF converter work?
videoToGif.answer: Choose a video, set the start and end points, pick a frame rate and width, then generate. The browser seeks through the selected range, paints each frame to a canvas and hands it to a local GIF encoder. The finished GIF is assembled in memory and downloaded from your device.

videoToGif.question: Is my video uploaded to a server?
videoToGif.answer: No. The file is opened with the File API, decoded by the browser's own video element and encoded on your machine. No frame, filename or file size is transmitted. The tool also works offline once the page has loaded.

videoToGif.question: How long can the clip be?
videoToGif.answer: There is no fixed time limit, but GIF grows quickly. Keep clips short, lower the frame rate and reduce the width for the smallest file. The tool estimates the frame count and warns you before a very large encode.

videoToGif.question: What frame rate should I choose?
videoToGif.answer: 10 to 15 fps feels smooth for most memes and reactions while keeping files small. Use 5 to 8 fps for slideshows or subtle motion, and 20 to 30 fps only for short, high-motion clips.

videoToGif.question: What do quality, dithering and ping-pong do?
videoToGif.answer: Quality controls the GIF palette search - a lower number means better colours and a larger file. Dithering adds a fine pattern that hides colour banding. Ping-pong plays the clip forward and then backward, which is popular for reaction GIFs.

videoToGif.question: What is the demo clip?
videoToGif.answer: Every field starts empty. The demo button draws a three-second animated test card on a canvas, records it with MediaRecorder on your device and loads it as a normal video, so you can try trimming and encoding without picking a file.

resumeBuilder.question: How does the Resume Builder work?
resumeBuilder.answer: Fill in the form on the left and watch the A4 or US Letter preview update instantly. Add, remove and reorder experience, education, skills and other sections, choose a template and accent colour, then print or save a vector PDF from your browser. Everything is stored in local storage and can be exported as a JSON project.

resumeBuilder.question: Is my personal data uploaded anywhere?
resumeBuilder.answer: No. Your name, contact details, photo and work history stay in this browser tab and in local storage on your device. The page makes no upload request and does not require an account. Export a JSON backup or print a PDF to keep a copy.

resumeBuilder.question: Is the resume ATS-friendly?
resumeBuilder.answer: The Minimal template is intentionally plain: one column, real text, no tables, icons or graphics in the body. All templates use selectable text rather than images, so applicant tracking systems can read names, roles, dates and bullet points. Always check the final PDF in the job board preview.

resumeBuilder.question: Why is everything blank at the start?
resumeBuilder.answer: No sample candidate is pre-filled for you. The editor opens empty; use the Load demo data button to explore a complete example, then clear it and replace every field with your own details.

resumeBuilder.question: How do I save a PDF?
resumeBuilder.answer: Press Print / Save PDF. The tool opens a clean print window with only the resume, sets the correct page size and removes the editor chrome. In the browser print dialog choose Save as PDF, keep margins at none and enable background graphics for accent colours.

resumeBuilder.question: What is the job description match panel?
resumeBuilder.answer: Paste a job advert into the match panel and the tool compares its keywords with the text already in your resume. It highlights terms you already cover and suggests important words that are missing, helping you tailor the document without inventing experience.

shoeClothingSize.question: How does the shoe and clothing size converter work?
shoeClothingSize.answer: Choose a category, a region and a size, and the converter maps it across EU, UK, US, Mondopoint and centimetres. For a personal recommendation, enter a foot length or body measurements instead: the tool compares them with the size chart and suggests the closest match with a fit note.

shoeClothingSize.question: Why can the same size fit differently between brands?
shoeClothingSize.answer: Size labels are not standardised. Last shape, fabric stretch, vanity sizing and regional grading all change the real measurements. Use the brand-specific fit offset in the tool and trust the garment's own measurement chart over the label whenever it is available.

shoeClothingSize.question: How should I measure my foot?
shoeClothingSize.answer: Stand on a sheet of paper with your heel against a wall, mark the longest toe, and measure the distance in centimetres. Do it late in the day when feet are slightly larger, measure both feet and use the longer one. Add about 0.5–1 cm of toe room for everyday shoes.

shoeClothingSize.question: How do kids' sizes work?
shoeClothingSize.answer: Children's shoe sizes grow quickly, so measure every few months rather than relying on age. Clothing is usually grouped by height in centimetres in Europe and by age in the US and UK. The converter includes child ranges, but height and chest measurements are more reliable than an age label.

shoeClothingSize.question: Can I build my own conversion chart?
shoeClothingSize.answer: Yes. Add your own rows with the size in each system and the matching centimetres, then reorder or delete them. The custom chart can be exported as CSV or printed as a PDF so a shop or tailor can keep a copy.

shoeClothingSize.question: Is anything uploaded or stored?
shoeClothingSize.answer: No. Conversions and custom charts are calculated in your browser. Your measurements and chart are saved only in local storage on this device, and clearing the tool removes them.

printSize.question: How do I convert pixels to print size?
printSize.answer: Divide the pixel count by the DPI to get inches, then multiply by 25.4 for millimetres. A 3000 × 2400 px file at 300 DPI prints at 10 × 8 inches. The calculator does this in both directions and also reports the effective PPI for any chosen paper size.

printSize.question: What DPI should I use for print?
printSize.answer: 300 PPI is the usual target for photographs and detailed art viewed up close. Large posters can be 150 PPI or lower because they are seen from further away, while line art and small text benefit from 300–600 PPI. Always confirm the printer's requirement before exporting.

printSize.question: What are bleed and safe margins?
printSize.answer: Bleed is extra artwork beyond the trim line, usually 3 mm, so small cutting errors do not leave a white edge. The safe margin keeps text and logos away from the trim, commonly 3–5 mm. The preview shows both on your chosen paper size.

printSize.question: Does the tool change my image file?
printSize.answer: No. It is a specification calculator: it tells you the pixel dimensions, DPI and paper size you need. Use an image editor or the ToolsTrek image resizer to produce the file, then check the result here before sending it to print.

printSize.question: Which paper size should I choose?
printSize.answer: A4 is the standard in most of the world, US Letter in the United States and Canada, and A3 or larger for posters. Photo sizes such as 4 × 6, 5 × 7 and 8 × 10 are common for prints. You can also enter a completely custom width and height.

printSize.question: What if my image has the wrong aspect ratio?
printSize.answer: The calculator warns when the image ratio does not match the paper. Cropping fills the page but loses edges; fitting adds white margins. Choose deliberately and keep the subject away from the crop line.

freelanceRate.question: How is the freelance hourly rate calculated?
freelanceRate.answer: The tool starts with the income you need after business costs, then adds overheads, tax, pension and holiday cover, and divides the total by the hours you can realistically bill. Billable capacity is deliberately lower than working hours because admin, sales and unpaid revisions take time.

freelanceRate.question: Why is a freelance rate higher than an employee salary?
freelanceRate.answer: A salary is only part of the cost of an employee: employers also pay pension, insurance, equipment and paid leave. A freelancer covers all of that plus unbilled time, sickness and gaps between contracts. The employee-to-contractor comparison makes the gap explicit.

freelanceRate.question: How many billable hours should I assume?
freelanceRate.answer: Many solo freelancers bill 50–70% of their working time. A 40-hour week with 25 billable hours is a realistic starting point; client work, proposals, invoicing and learning fill the rest. If you are new, be conservative — overestimating capacity produces an unsustainably low rate.

freelanceRate.question: What is value-based pricing?
freelanceRate.answer: Instead of charging for time, you price against the value the work creates for the client — more revenue, lower cost or reduced risk. The calculator includes a value-based scenario so you can compare a time-based floor with a project price that reflects the outcome.

freelanceRate.question: How should I quote a fixed-price project?
freelanceRate.answer: Estimate the hours honestly, add a risk buffer for revisions and unknowns, then multiply by your target hourly rate. Show the client the scope, deliverables and revision limit. A fixed price without a defined scope is how projects become unprofitable.

freelanceRate.question: Does the calculator include taxes?
freelanceRate.answer: It includes the tax and contribution rate you enter, which varies by country and legal structure. It is a planning model, not a tax return. Check local rules for VAT/GST, self-employment contributions and allowable expenses with an accountant.

businessCard.question: What size should a business card be?
businessCard.answer: In the US and Canada the standard is 3.5 × 2 inches (88.9 × 50.8 mm). In Europe, the UK and most of Asia, 85 × 55 mm is the norm. Square and slim formats are popular for creative studios, but always confirm the printer's trim size before ordering.

businessCard.question: How much bleed does a business card need?
businessCard.answer: Add 3 mm (0.125 in) of bleed on every edge when any colour or image runs to the edge. That makes the document 94.9 × 56.8 mm for a US card and 91 × 61 mm for a European card. Keep text at least 3–4 mm inside the trim line.

businessCard.question: Can I export a print-ready PDF?
businessCard.answer: Yes. The export renders your design at 300 DPI and places it on a page sized to your card or card back. When crop marks are enabled, the PDF adds a margin and corner marks so a print shop can trim the job accurately.

businessCard.question: How many cards fit on one sheet?
businessCard.answer: It depends on the card and sheet size, the gap between cards and the sheet margin. With a US card and a 4 mm gap on A4, the layout section shows the exact grid and copy count. Adjust the gap or margin to see how many more fit.

businessCard.question: Can I add a QR code to my card?
businessCard.answer: Yes. Enter any URL, email address, phone number or plain text and the maker generates a QR code locally. It is embedded in the preview, the PNG and the PDF. Test-scan the exported file before sending it to print.

businessCard.question: What paper and finish should I choose?
businessCard.answer: 350–400 gsm card stock feels substantial without becoming brittle. A matte or soft-touch laminate is easy to write on, while a gloss finish makes colours pop. Spot UV, foil and letterpress add cost, so ask for a proof before a large run.

businessCard.question: Is my logo uploaded to a server?
businessCard.answer: No. The logo and contact details never leave your browser. Everything is rendered on your device and saved to local storage so you can pick up where you left off.

businessCard.question: Can I reuse the design later?
businessCard.answer: Yes. Export the project as JSON from the maker. It stores your brand details, colours, template choices and print settings so you can import it on another device or hand it to a colleague. The logo is included in the file when you add one.

letterhead.question: What size should a letterhead be?
letterhead.answer: A4 (210 × 297 mm) is the standard in most of the world and US Letter (8.5 × 11 in) in the United States and Canada. A5 is useful for short notes and compliments slips. Choose the same paper your printer stocks so the final trim and margins match your proof.

letterhead.question: How much margin and bleed should a letterhead use?
letterhead.answer: Keep at least 15–20 mm of clear margin for body copy and leave room for a signature. Add 3 mm of bleed on every edge when a colour band or image runs to the edge. The preview marks the trim and safe area so nothing important is clipped.

letterhead.question: Can I export a print-ready PDF?
letterhead.answer: Yes. The letterhead is rendered at 300 DPI on a page sized to A4, US Letter, A5 or your chosen paper. With crop marks enabled, the PDF adds a margin and corner marks so a print shop can trim accurately.

letterhead.question: What should a letterhead include?
letterhead.answer: The company name and logo, a postal address, phone number, email, website and any registration or tax details your market requires. Keep the footer compact so the body copy has room to breathe, and leave a clear signature area at the end.

letterhead.question: Can I match the letterhead to my business card?
letterhead.answer: Yes. Use the same brand colour, ink colour, typeface and logo. The Business Card Maker uses the same design tokens, so you can build a matching card and letterhead without a separate design file. Layouts can differ to suit the format.

letterhead.question: Is my logo uploaded to a server?
letterhead.answer: No. The logo, company details and letter copy never leave your browser. Everything is rendered on your device and saved to local storage so you can pick up where you left off.

letterhead.question: Can I reuse the design later?
letterhead.answer: Yes. Export the project as JSON and import it on another device or hand it to a colleague. It stores the brand details, colours, template choice, paper size and letter content. The logo is included in the file when you add one.

letterhead.question: Can I write the letter inside the tool?
letterhead.answer: Yes. Add a recipient block, subject, body, closing and signature, and the preview shows exactly what will export. Leave those fields blank if you only need a blank letterhead to print and write on later.

configFileGenerator.question: What does the Config File Generator produce?
configFileGenerator.answer: Four files: a .gitignore assembled from selectable stacks and custom rules, a robots.txt with crawl directives and a sitemap reference, an HTML block of SEO and social meta tags, and an Apache .htaccess file with security, compression, caching and redirect rules.

configFileGenerator.question: Does .gitignore untrack files that are already committed?
configFileGenerator.answer: No. It only stops untracked files from being added. Run git rm --cached <file> to stop tracking an existing file, then commit the removal. If a secret was committed, rotate it immediately — deleting it from the latest commit does not remove it from history.

configFileGenerator.question: Is robots.txt a security control?
configFileGenerator.answer: No. It is a request that well-behaved crawlers honour, not access control. Anyone can read the file and ignore it. Protect private pages with authentication, noindex headers or server rules, and never list sensitive paths in robots.txt.

configFileGenerator.question: Will .htaccess work on my server?
configFileGenerator.answer: .htaccess is read by Apache and LiteSpeed. Nginx ignores it and needs equivalent rules in the server block. Some managed hosts disable overrides. Test on staging and keep a backup, because a malformed rule can take the site offline.

configFileGenerator.question: Can I save different configurations?
configFileGenerator.answer: Yes. Each tab can be saved as a named preset in local storage, and presets can be applied or deleted independently. You can also download a single file or all populated files as a ZIP bundle.

configFileGenerator.question: Are the generated files uploaded anywhere?
configFileGenerator.answer: No. Everything is generated from your selections in the browser, and the ZIP is assembled locally with JSZip. No account is required and no configuration is sent to a server.

subtitleEditor.question: How do I fix subtitles that are out of sync?
subtitleEditor.answer: If every cue is early or late by the same amount, use Shift every cue with a positive or negative offset. If the drift grows over time, the file was probably made at a different frame rate: use the FPS converter to scale the whole timeline. For one bad cue, edit its start and end times directly.

subtitleEditor.question: What is the difference between SRT and VTT?
subtitleEditor.answer: SRT is the older, widely supported format with a cue number, a comma-separated timestamp and plain text. WebVTT starts with WEBVTT, uses a dot before milliseconds and supports styling and positioning. Both are exported as UTF-8 so Unicode text survives.

subtitleEditor.question: What reading speed should I aim for?
subtitleEditor.answer: Around 15–20 characters per second is comfortable, up to about 25 for short cues. Keep cues to one or two lines of roughly 42 characters and on screen for at least 0.6 seconds. The validator flags anything above your chosen limits.

subtitleEditor.question: Can I preview subtitles against my video?
subtitleEditor.answer: Yes. Add a local video file and the editor plays it with the active cue overlaid. The video is read directly from your device with a temporary object URL and is never uploaded or saved. Jump to any cue with its play button.

subtitleEditor.question: Which formats can I export?
subtitleEditor.answer: SRT, WebVTT, CSV for spreadsheets and translation workflows, a plain transcript with timecodes, and a JSON project file that can be re-imported. Copying the SRT to the clipboard is also supported.

subtitleEditor.question: Is my subtitle file uploaded?
subtitleEditor.answer: No. Parsing, retiming, validation and export all run in your browser. The cue list autosaves in local storage on this device, and clearing the editor removes it.

babyGrowthFeeding.question: How are the growth percentiles calculated?
babyGrowthFeeding.answer: Each measurement is compared with a WHO-aligned monthly reference for the baby's sex. The z-score is (measurement − median) ÷ standard deviation, and the percentile is the area under the normal curve below that z-score. Months between rows are interpolated. The tables are simplified for education; your clinician's charts remain the authority.

babyGrowthFeeding.question: What does the 50th percentile mean?
babyGrowthFeeding.answer: It is the median: half of healthy children of the same age and sex are above it and half below. A baby on the 15th percentile who follows that line is growing normally. The trend across visits matters far more than one number.

babyGrowthFeeding.question: Should I use corrected age for a premature baby?
babyGrowthFeeding.answer: For babies born before 37 weeks, corrected age subtracts the weeks they were early. Many clinicians use it for growth and development until about 24 months. Enter the gestational age and the calculator shows both, letting you switch which one drives the percentiles.

babyGrowthFeeding.question: How much milk does a baby need?
babyGrowthFeeding.answer: A common guide is about 150 ml per kilogram per day, split across the number of feeds. Breastfed babies feed on demand and do not need measured volumes; the figure is an estimate, not a target to force. Always mix formula exactly as the tin instructs.

babyGrowthFeeding.question: When should solids start?
babyGrowthFeeding.answer: Around 6 months, and not before about 4 months. Readiness signs matter more than the date: good head control, sitting with support, reaching for food and losing the tongue-thrust reflex. Milk remains the main source of nutrition through the first year.

babyGrowthFeeding.question: Is this medical advice?
babyGrowthFeeding.answer: No. It is an educational calculator for understanding growth trends and feeding arithmetic. Speak to a paediatrician, health visitor or dietitian if a baby loses weight, crosses two percentile lines, feeds poorly or has fewer wet nappies.

babyGrowthFeeding.question: Is my baby's data uploaded?
babyGrowthFeeding.answer: No. The profile, measurements and feeding settings stay in local storage in this browser. PDF and CSV exports are generated on your device, and clearing the tool removes the saved data.
